abstract: Cystic fibrosis (CF) causes severely damaged pancreatic morphology and cystic fibrosis-related diabetes (CFRD), but the cellular drivers of CFRD in the pancreas are not understood. Here, we perform single-cell and spatial profiling of 2.04 M cells from 23 non-disease or CF pancreas donors. A high-mucin ductal sub-type had relatively preserved abundance and genomic profiles but altered localization in CF. Changes in inflammatory and fibrotic pathways were driven by crosstalk between immune and pro-fibrotic cells in specific niches. Beta cells had extensive changes in CF, including increased stress responses and evidence for compensatory secretion, that were distinct from those in type 1 and type 2 diabetes. Islets localized near large adipose tissue and collagen in CF had reduced beta cells linked to signaling from adipocytes, macrophages, stellate cells, and high-mucin ductal cells. Overall, our results highlight pancreatic microenvironments of beta cell dysfunction in CF and offer in-roads to preserving beta cells in CFRD.
